comments.text: I have a vintage forest green one that was issued to Rangers from the U.S. Forest Service, and it’s consistently the jacket I reach for in the late fall/early winter.

I have a (single) Mackinaw Cruiser and a Mackinaw Jac Shirt, both Filson. The latter has a cotton lining and in many ways I rate it as the better all round item (warmer, more coat like) and it's less expensive too (though not made in the US)

I don’t really see a valid argument for having a liner in this jacket for comfort. Any time it’s cold enough outside to wear a double mac (or even a regular mac), you’ll be wearing a sweater or at least some kind of long sleeve shirt. These are meant to be a final outer layer, not something to just throw on with a t-shirt.

Filson has been renaming some of their classics.  The "new" Double Mackinaw is called the "Mackinaw Wool Cape Coat" & there are some clear differences.  No more:  double layered sleeves, double hand pockets, game/map pouch, shell holders & lastly no more buttons in lieu of snaps.  Massive decrease in quality.
Weatherwool:  Ive had 2 AAJ's (their answer to the double mack) & there is no comparison really.  WW's wool is the nicest wool Ive ever touched in my life.. by a LOT!  The build quality is what you'd expect for the price & more.  If you've got the means, you wont regret it.
